title: Emission economics fingerprint and KV-credit attribution pipeline
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a production-safe pipeline and lightweight runtime probes to attribute per-token latency and cost impact, explicitly accounting for KV/prefix cache hits, prefetch credits, and batched execution. This ticket covers:

1) Runtime probe spec: minimal per-token events emitted inline with request traces (start/end timestamps per emission step, cache-hit boolean, batch-id). Must keep overhead <3% p99 latency and max 200 bytes additional payload per request for sampled traces.

2) Ingestion pipeline: Kafka topic + dedup filter, enrichment service to join trace/event with request metadata (model variant, sequence length, route, tenant), aggregation into hourly and sliding-window rollups for cost attribution.

3) Attribution model: combine kernel timing deltas, batch amortization rules, and cache-hit discounts to compute an attributable token-cost and token-latency contribution per request. Produce schema for billing reconciliation and SLA backfill.

4) Dashboards & Alerts: Grafana panels for per-model per-route token-latency, KV hit distribution, and regressions vs baseline. Alert when average token-cost increases >10% for 1h with >5% traffic impact.

5) Rollout plan: opt-in tracing (config flag at route level), sample 1% by default then scale via adaptive sampling based on traffic and error windows. Backwards compatible: if probes absent, fall back to coarse request-level attribution.

Non-goals: full per-subtoken linguistic attribution (out of scope for phase 1).

Success criteria: end-to-end pipeline with <2s median ingestion latency, sampling overhead <2% p99 latency increase, dashboards showing KV-hit-adjusted token-cost, and a reconciler job that maps sample-derived attributions to billing-level summaries.
comments: 2026-03-11 — Asha Patel: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to keep runtime probe as a binary-compatible header and an in-memory event buffer to avoid extra RPCs. Action: Jonah to draft the probe protobuf + size budget.

2026-03-12 — Jonah Kim: Initial probe spec PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1928 — includes event schema (token_index, phase, ts_ns, kv_hit). Needs review for: a) privacy (no prompt content), b) performance (serialize with msgpack).

2026-03-12 — Security review (Marina Lopez): flagged potential PII leakage if token_index is correlated with prompt offsets in customer logs. Recommendation: strip any prompt offsets when storing long-term; only keep relative indices in ephemeral buffer. Marking security_review_required: true.

2026-03-13 — Data Eng (Kunal Rao): pipeline sketch — use topic redwood.token-attrib.v1, enrichment lambda to join with request metadata from request-store. Concern: high-cardinality tenant tags producing many series in Prometheus; suggested using cardinality-reduction by bucketing slow tokens into quantiles for dashboards.

2026-03-13 — Jonah Kim: Implemented sampling controller prototype (adaptive sampler) — linked test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-tools/commit/4f2b9a. Early results: at 1% sampling, we see stable estimates for median token-latency but tail estimates require 2.5% for 99th percentile accuracy within 5% error.

2026-03-14 — PM review (Elena Ruiz): Approved rollout canary to 5% for internal tenants after performance validation. PM asks to include a dashboard panel showing sampling weight and confidence intervals for the attributed metrics.
